deliverables.title: Twelve artifacts. Not twelve paragraphs of chat.
deliverables.body: Every stage produces a structured, editable, versioned document — the same set an engineering team would spend weeks assembling by hand.

requirements.title: Requirements
requirements.body: Functional and non-functional requirements, user roles, and the flows between them — traceable back to your interview answers.

architecture.title: System architecture
architecture.body: An architecture pattern, a justified tech stack, and the services that make it up. Ask "why this?" on any choice and get the rationale, tradeoffs, and alternatives.

database.title: Database schema
database.body: Entities, columns, types, and relations — as an ER diagram and as runnable PostgreSQL DDL.

diagrams.title: Diagrams & canvas
diagrams.body: ER, architecture, and per-endpoint sequence diagrams, plus an interactive canvas. Export to Mermaid, Draw.io, SVG, PNG, or PDF.

vision.title: Product vision
vision.body: The PM's view of your idea: problem, target users, value proposition, and success metrics — ready to put in front of a stakeholder.

api.title: REST API design
api.body: Endpoints, request and response schemas, and status codes — with an interactive OpenAPI explorer and a Postman collection.

review.title: AI architect review
review.body: Your design, scored on security, scalability, performance, and cost, with findings per category and a critical-issues callout.

roadmap.title: Implementation roadmap
roadmap.body: Phases, milestones, and tasks with effort estimates — the plan you actually build against.

cost.title: Hosting cost estimate
cost.body: A projected monthly bill across 8 providers at 100, 1,000, and 10,000 users, with the cheapest option per scale. Calculated, not guessed.

threat.title: Threat model
threat.body: A STRIDE security analysis of your design — every threat with its component, severity, and a concrete mitigation.

qa.title: Test & QA plan
qa.body: A testing strategy with named test cases grouped by type — unit, integration, e2e, security, performance, and acceptance.

scaffold.title: Code scaffold
scaffold.body: A runnable NestJS + Prisma backend generated from your design — download the ZIP or push it straight to a new GitHub repo.

problem.title: Going from idea to a real architecture is where projects stall.
problem.body: Founders and teams know what they want to build — but turning that into requirements, a database, an API, and a defensible architecture is slow, manual, and easy to get wrong.

blank.title: The blank-page problem
blank.body: You have the idea, but staring at an empty doc — requirements, schema, endpoints — is where momentum dies. Most people never get past it.

slow.title: Weeks of back-and-forth
slow.body: Scoping meetings, spec drafts, diagram tools, review cycles. It takes weeks to reach a design a team can actually build from.

costly.title: Expensive to get wrong
costly.body: A weak schema or a missed non-functional requirement surfaces in production. Rework, hiring a consultant, or rebuilding costs real time and money.

q1.q: Is this just another AI chatbot?
q1.a: No. Archivato is an architecture engine. Instead of a wall of chat text, it produces structured, versioned, editable artifacts — requirements, schema, API, review, roadmap — the exact things a team builds from.

q2.q: Do I need to be technical to use it?
q2.a: No. You describe your idea in plain language and answer a short interview. Archivato handles the technical translation into requirements, database, and API design — which you can then edit or hand to a developer.

q3.q: What do I actually get out of it?
q3.a: A complete, editable system design: a requirements document, system architecture, database schema with diagrams, a REST API, a scored architect review, and an implementation roadmap — exportable to JSON, Markdown, OpenAPI, or a scaffolded repo.

q4.q: What's the difference between Free and Pro?
q4.a: Free covers one project through the interview, requirements, system and database design, and Product Vision. Pro unlocks the API design, AI review, roadmap, cost estimate, and export — for up to five projects.

q5.q: Can I edit what the AI generates?
q5.a: Yes. Every artifact is directly editable through structured forms — not free text — and you can refine the whole design by chat. Every change is versioned so you can compare and restore any point.

q6.a: The interface is available in English and Arabic (with full right-to-left support), and the interview adapts its questions to the language of your idea.
